answer=1 raw='<think>The FTCS (Forward Time Central Space) scheme for the one-dimensional wave equation: u_tt = c² u_xx.

The standard discretization:
(u_j^{n+1} - 2u_j^n + u_j^{n-1})/Δt² = c² (u_{j+1}^n - 2u_j^n + u_{j-1}^n)/Δx²

This is actually the leapfrog scheme for the wave equation, not really FTCS. FTCS typically refers to forward time, central space for first-order PDEs.

Wait, let me reconsider. For the wave equation, the "FTCS" scheme often refers to:
u_j^{n+1} = 2u_j^n - u_j^{n-1} + (cΔt/Δx)² (u_{j+1}^n - 2u_j^n + u_{j-1}^n)

This scheme is consistent with the wave equation.

For stability, using von Neumann analysis with u_j^n = ξ^n e^{ikjΔx}:
ξ² - 2ξ + 1 = -μ²(2 - 2cos(kΔx)) where μ = cΔt/Δx
ξ² - 2ξ + 1 + 2μ²(1-cos(kΔx)) = 0
ξ = 1 ± √(-2μ²(1-cos(kΔx)))
ξ = 1 ± iμ√(2(1-cos(kΔx)))
ξ = 1 ± i·2μ·sin(kΔx/2)

|ξ|² = 1 + 4μ²sin²(kΔx/2)

This is always > 1, so the scheme is unconditionally unstable!

So the answer is 1: Consistent, unconditionally unstable.</think>
